question: Not shared (condition 1 fails on the population class). Both label the task MCI against controls from resting-state fMRI, but P-360's positive class is MCI secondary to end-stage renal disease: 51 hospital patients (mean age 50) with ESRD, a cognitive impairment the paper attributes to uraemia, dialysis and related causes, against 39 middle-aged volunteers. P-55's is MCI among older adults (mean age 69) against age-matched controls at a mental health centre. As with Parkinson's MCI against Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI, or MCI in diabetic inpatients against dust-exposed miners (C-180), these are different population classes behind the same label. The channel (fMRI) and metric match.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (match); both also report AUC.

figures.P-360: DHMR dynamic functional networks, 87 t-test-selected edges, linear SVM, LOOCV on 90 subjects (51 ESRDaMCI/39 normal): accuracy 88.5670 +/- 0.3587%, AUC 0.9008. No interval for sampling uncertainty (the +/- is run-to-run). Wilson, n = 90: [0.804, 0.936]. Hanley-McNeil, AUC 0.9008 with 51/39: Q1 = 0.8195, Q2 = 0.8538, SE = 0.0325, CI [0.837, 0.965]. All hyper-parameters were tuned by LOOCV on the same sample.
figures.P-55: Postcentral-gyrus VMHC (single feature), RBF SVM, leave-one-out on 121 subjects (53 MCI/68 HC): printed accuracy 63.64% (= 77/121), sensitivity 71.69%, specificity 89.71%, AUC 68.42%. Wilson for 63.64%, n = 121: [0.548, 0.717]. The printed accuracy is inconsistent with the printed sensitivity and specificity, which imply 38/53 + 61/68 = 99/121 = 81.82% (Wilson [0.740, 0.877]). Hanley-McNeil, AUC 0.6842 with 53/68: SE = 0.0494, CI [0.587, 0.781].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure: neither paper reports its method in the other's population or with the other's feature set. P-360's static Pearson-correlation networks reach 80.07% in its own Table 6, which shows that feature construction alone moves accuracy by several points within one cohort, but that is not the other paper's condition.
performance_validity: Neither study is near ceiling (88.57% and AUC 0.90; 63.64% and AUC 0.68). Both estimates are optimistic by design: P-360 tunes window length, step, k and regularisation by LOOCV on the same 90 subjects, and P-55 chose the VMHC cluster by a whole-sample group t-test before its leave-one-out classification.
reason: The figures differ beyond uncertainty on accuracy (88.57% [0.804, 0.936] against 63.64% [0.548, 0.717]) and AUC. But the two papers classify different populations under the MCI label: MCI secondary to end-stage renal disease in dialysis-age patients (mean 50 years) against older adults with MCI (mean 69 years). Condition 1 fails whatever the numbers show. P-55's printed accuracy is also inconsistent with its own sensitivity and specificity, which imply 81.82%, and the gap would narrow to one direction on that figure.

quotes.quote: Fifty-one patients with ESRD who had been diagnosed with MCI (ESRDaMCI group) were included in the study.
The structure and function of brain networks have been altered in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD).
The best ACC, SPE, and AUC are 88.5670% ± 0.3587%, 90.3577% ± 0.5461% and 0.9008 ± 0.0011, respectively.
The remaining 53 MCI patients and 68 age-, sex- and education-matched HCs were included in the final analyses
ultimately yielding respective accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC values of 63.64 %, 71.69 %, 89.71 %, and 68.42 %.
